title: Meridian Health Loop — SOC 2 Type II readiness assessment
client: Meridian Health Loop, Inc. — a 45-person healthcare communications technology startup. Its platform delivers patient workflows over SMS/web/voice on behalf of health systems: ER discharge follow-up, clinical study enrollment, and appointment check-in are the flagship workflow templates. It processes PHI as a business associate. Two flagship health-system prospects (St. Aldric Health and Bayview Regional Health Network) have made a Q1 2027 SOC 2 Type II report a condition of contract expansion.
consultant_role: Senior consultant at Ledgerline Assurance LLC engaged to run a SOC 2 Type II readiness assessment ahead of the Q1 2027 audit. The engagement director is Katherine Liu; the readiness deliverables go to Meridian's CEO and CTO and frame the remediation program for the proposed review period 2026-10-01 through 2027-03-31.

cast.name: Dana Okafor
cast.reliability_note: Commercially candid; sponsors the readiness engagement because St. Aldric and Bayview demanded it. Defers on technical detail; occasionally repeats the marketing line about compliance posture.

cast.name: Priya Raman
cast.reliability_note: Deep on architecture but systematically optimistic in written memos: her May 2026 architecture memo overclaims encryption-at-rest coverage and subprocessor hygiene. Concedes specifics under direct questioning in interview. Trust her topology, verify her control assertions against exports.

cast.reliability_note: The most candid internal voice on infrastructure reality — admits the DR plan has never been tested, the legacy VPN has no MFA, and the snapshot bucket predates default encryption. His interview and runbook are authoritative for current-state infra.

cast.role: DevOps Engineer II, Meridian Health Loop
cast.reliability_note: CONFIDENTLY WRONG JUNIOR VOICE. Three PHI-bearing buckets — meridian-db-snapshots, meridian-legacy-exports, and meridian-data-lake-raw — sit on the account-default SSE-S3 key, not the customer-managed KMS keys the memo claims and POL-09 requires. meridian-db-snapshots also has public-access-block disabled, and account-default encryption gates nothing: Graphite Wren read plaintext PHI snapshots from it with the leaked over-permissive IAM key (VB-2026-C1). The runbook confirms the bucket was carved out of the 2024 KMS migration and never migrated back.
contradictions.why_decidable: The bucket inventory is a raw system export dated 2026-06-08 (Gideon Hart's cover note marks it as pulled directly from the AWS API); the memo is undated narrative prose. Export beats assertion; the runbook and the pen-test critical independently confirm both the off-standard key and the exploitability.

rules: Attestation language: SOC 2 is an attestation, not a certification. The words 'certified' and 'certification' must not appear anywhere in a Ledgerline deliverable — including when characterizing third-party claims (paraphrase, e.g. 'the press release overstates Meridian's attestation status'). Never state or imply that Meridian 'is SOC 2 compliant'; readiness deliverables state gaps against criteria, not compliance conclusions.
Evidence citation: every gap finding in the report must cite at least one evidence document inline using the exact format '(source: <filename>)', e.g. '(source: access_review_export_2026-06-08.csv)'.
Criteria identifiers: reference Trust Services Criteria with AICPA 2017 (2022 revision) identifiers in uppercase dot notation — CC6.1, A1.2, C1.1 — in both deliverables.

Controlled vocabularies: control status uses exactly implemented | partial | gap (lowercase); remediation priority uses exactly P1 | P2 | P3. No other status or priority words (e.g. 'compliant', 'non-compliant', 'critical priority') may be used in the matrix columns.
Dates and numbers: all dates in ISO YYYY-MM-DD; percentages carry the % sign; US spelling throughout.
Scoping discipline: no criterion category may be declared in scope or out of scope without citing the customer-contract clause or business rationale that drives the call.
